claim: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves task accuracy in decision-making LLMs but produces extremely overconfident models, while supervised fine-tuning (SFT) yields substantially better calibration (including under distribution shift) at the cost of smaller accuracy gains.
stance_target: Fine-tuning paradigm choice (RL vs. supervised) drives a calibration-accuracy tradeoff in LLMs
scope_conditions: Decision-making LLM tasks, comparing SFT and RLVR fine-tuning paradigms
quoted_support: We show that while RLVR improves task performance, it produces extremely overconfident models, whereas SFT yields substantially better calibration, even under distribution shift, though with smaller performance gains.

claim: RLVR's overconfidence failure arises because decision tokens act as extraction steps in reasoning traces and do not carry confidence information, preventing the RL objective from surfacing calibrated alternatives.
stance_target: Mechanistic explanation for why RL-trained LLMs become overconfident
scope_conditions: Diagnostic experiments on decision-token probability structure in RLVR-trained models
quoted_support: we diagnose RLVR's failure, showing that decision tokens act as extraction steps of the decision in reasoning traces and do not carry confidence information, which prevents reinforcement learning from surfacing calibrated alternatives.

claim: A proposed calibration-aware reinforcement learning formulation that directly adjusts decision-token probabilities preserves RLVR's accuracy level while reducing Expected Calibration Error (ECE) by up to 9 points.
stance_target: Calibration-aware RL objectives can resolve the RLVR accuracy-calibration tradeoff without sacrificing accuracy
scope_conditions: Proposed method evaluated against standard RLVR baseline
quoted_support: we propose a calibration-aware reinforcement learning formulation that directly adjusts decision-token probabilities. Our method preserves RLVR's accuracy level while mitigating overconfidence, reducing ECE scores up to 9 points.
